Section 1 of 14

Can People Really Change?

Have you ever promised yourself that things would be different?

You may have decided to stop a harmful habit, control your temper, repair a relationship, or become more disciplined. For a while, you did well. Then stress returned, an old trigger appeared, or you made the same choice again.

Repeated failure can make change feel impossible.

People may also place labels on you because of your past:

Addicted.

Angry.

Unreliable.

Broken.

Too far gone.

The Creator sees your past, but He also sees the person you can become through His power.

Jesus does more than forgive what you have done. He offers to change who you are becoming.

What Does It Mean to Become New?

Read 2 Corinthians 5:17 ↗.

The Bible says that anyone who is connected to Jesus becomes a new creation.

This does not mean your memories, personality, family connections, or Native identity disappear. The Creator is restoring you, not erasing you.

Becoming new means that Jesus gives you:

  • A new relationship with the Creator
  • A new foundation for your identity
  • New desires
  • New spiritual strength
  • A new direction
  • A new purpose
  • A new future

Your past may help explain where you have been, but it does not have to decide where you are going.

Why Is Changing Our Behavior Not Enough?

Rules can control outward behavior for a while. Fear of consequences can make us hide certain actions. The desire to impress people can make us appear better than we are.

But outward change does not always reach the heart.

A person may stop speaking angry words while still feeding hatred inside. Someone may appear honest while secretly looking for the next opportunity to deceive. A person may perform religious actions while remaining proud, selfish, or cruel.

Jesus wants to change more than appearances.

Read Matthew 23:25–28 ↗.

Jesus confronted people who looked righteous outwardly but were corrupt within. He taught that real change begins in the heart.

We do not simply need better behavior. We need new hearts.

The Creator Promises a New Heart

Read Ezekiel 36:25–27 ↗.

God promises to cleanse us, remove the hard heart, and give us a new one. He also promises to place His Spirit within us.

A hard heart resists the Creator. It protects old wounds, excuses harmful choices, and refuses correction.

A new heart becomes open to truth. It can feel compassion, receive forgiveness, admit wrong, and desire the Creator’s way.

You cannot perform heart surgery on yourself.

The Creator must do this work in you.

What Does It Mean to Be Born Again?

Read John 3:1–8 ↗.

Nicodemus was educated, respected, and religious. Yet Jesus told him that he needed to be born again.

Jesus was not speaking about another physical birth. He was describing a new spiritual beginning created by the Holy Spirit.

Physical birth gives us physical life. The new birth gives us spiritual life.

At the new birth:

  • You recognize your need for the Creator.
  • You turn away from sin.
  • You trust Jesus as your Savior.
  • God forgives and accepts you.
  • The Holy Spirit begins living and working within you.
  • Your life receives a new direction.

You may experience strong emotions when this happens, or you may not. The new birth rests on the Creator’s promise rather than a particular feeling.

Does Change Happen Immediately?

Some changes can happen quickly. A person may immediately lose the desire for a certain habit or find unexpected strength to make a difficult choice.

Other changes happen slowly.

Read Mark 4:26–29 ↗.

Jesus compared spiritual growth to a seed. A healthy plant is alive from the moment it begins to grow, but it does not become mature overnight.

Your relationship with the Creator works in a similar way.

When you give your life to Jesus, you are fully accepted. You also begin a lifelong process of growth.

The Bible calls this process sanctification.

Read 1 Thessalonians 4:3 ↗ and Philippians 1:6 ↗.

Sanctification means that the Creator is setting you apart for Himself and gradually shaping your character to become more like Jesus.

You do not have to finish the process before God accepts you. You grow because He has already welcomed you.

Who Produces the Change?

Read Philippians 2:12–13 ↗.

The Creator works within you, giving you both the desire and the ability to follow Him.

You still make real choices. God does not take over your mind or remove your freedom. The Holy Spirit teaches, convicts, strengthens, and invites. You decide whether to cooperate.

Think about a canoe moving with a strong current. You still hold the paddle and choose your direction, but you are no longer trying to move forward through your strength alone.

Spiritual growth is a partnership in which the Creator supplies the power and you choose to respond.

The Spirit Produces New Fruit

Read Galatians 5:16–25 ↗.

The passage contrasts two ways of living.

One life is controlled by selfish desires. It produces sexual sin, hatred, jealousy, angry outbursts, division, envy, drunkenness, and other destructive behaviors.

The other life is guided by the Holy Spirit. It produces:

  • Love
  • Joy
  • Peace
  • Patience
  • Kindness
  • Goodness
  • Faithfulness
  • Gentleness
  • Self-control

Fruit grows from what a plant is connected to.

You do not create spiritual fruit by pretending to be patient, peaceful, or loving. These qualities grow as you remain connected to Jesus and allow His Spirit to work within you.

Stay Connected to Jesus

Read John 15:1–5 ↗.

Jesus compared Himself to a vine and His followers to branches.

A branch separated from the vine cannot produce fruit. In the same way, lasting change is impossible when we try to live apart from Jesus.

Connection grows through:

  • Honest prayer
  • Regular time in Scripture
  • Responding to the Holy Spirit
  • Obeying what the Creator shows you
  • Remembering God’s promises
  • Spending time with people who encourage spiritual growth
  • Serving others

These actions do not earn the Creator’s love. They keep your heart open to the love and power He already offers.

The Creator Renews Your Mind

Read Romans 12:1–2 ↗.

Much of the battle for change takes place in your thoughts.

Repeated thoughts become familiar paths. Those thoughts influence desires, and desires influence choices. Choices repeated over time become habits.

The Holy Spirit renews your mind through truth.

When shame says, “You will always be your worst mistake,” Scripture says that you can become a new creation.

When temptation says, “You need this to feel whole,” Scripture says the Creator can satisfy your deepest need.

When resentment says, “Hold onto this forever,” Jesus offers strength to begin forgiving.

When fear says, “You are alone,” God promises His presence.

You cannot always stop a thought from entering your mind, but you can decide whether to welcome it, feed it, or replace it with truth.

Read Philippians 4:8 ↗.

Choose what you repeatedly place before your mind. What you watch, hear, read, and practice will influence the person you are becoming.

Does Becoming New Erase Your Culture?

The Creator does not renew people by turning them into copies of another race.

Read Revelation 7:9–10 ↗.

God’s future family includes people from every nation, tribe, language, and people. Their identities remain recognizable while they stand united before Him.

Every culture contains expressions of beauty, family, courage, generosity, creativity, and care. Every culture also contains human ideas and practices that must be examined in the light of Scripture.

That includes dominant American culture and religious culture.

Jesus calls every person to release whatever leads away from truth, love, purity, justice, and loyalty to the Creator. He also protects human dignity and gathers people without making them identical.

A new heart does not make you less Native. It helps you become the person the Creator intended you to be.

Can Patterns Passed Down Through Families Be Broken?

Families can pass down wonderful gifts: language, knowledge, stories, skills, humor, resilience, and ways of caring for one another.

Families can also pass down painful patterns.

Anger, silence, addiction, fear, neglect, dishonesty, or unhealthy ways of handling conflict can move from one generation to another.

These patterns are powerful, but they do not have to determine your future.

Read 1 Peter 1:18–19 ↗.

Jesus can free you from empty or harmful patterns received from the past.

This does not mean rejecting your family. It means allowing the Creator to heal what causes harm while preserving what reflects goodness and love.

With God’s help, a painful pattern can stop with you. A healthier story can begin through you.

What If You Are Fighting an Addiction?

Addiction can affect the body, thoughts, relationships, finances, and spiritual life. It often grows through repeated attempts to escape pain.

The Creator offers real power, but asking for help is not a sign of weak faith.

Read Ecclesiastes 4:9–10 ↗ and Galatians 6:2 ↗.

God often works through trusted people, recovery communities, counselors, medical professionals, and supportive relationships.

Bring the struggle into the light with someone safe. Remove easy access to what controls you. Learn your triggers. Replace the destructive habit with healthy action. Ask the Holy Spirit for strength one decision at a time.

Freedom may happen suddenly, or it may involve a long process of healing and accountability.

Jesus does not abandon people who are still learning how to be free.

Is Temptation the Same as Sin?

Read Hebrews 4:15 ↗.

Jesus experienced temptation, but He did not sin.

Being tempted does not mean you have already failed. Temptation is an invitation to move away from the Creator. Sin occurs when we welcome that invitation and choose it.

Read James 1:13–15 ↗.

Notice the path described in this passage:

  • A harmful desire attracts your attention.
  • You continue feeding it.
  • The desire leads to a choice.
  • The repeated choice produces destruction.

The earlier you interrupt that process, the stronger your response can be.

When temptation comes:

  1. Recognize it honestly.
  2. Ask the Creator for immediate help.
  3. Recall a clear Bible promise.
  4. Move away from the situation if possible.
  5. Contact someone who supports your decision.
  6. Choose a healthy action in its place.

Read 1 Corinthians 10:13 ↗.

The Creator promises to provide a way through temptation. Look for that way and take it.

What If You Fail Again?

Growth does not mean you will never struggle or stumble.

Peter promised that he would remain loyal to Jesus. A few hours later, he denied knowing Him three times.

Read Luke 22:54–62 ↗.

Peter failed badly, but Jesus did not discard him.

Read John 21:15–17 ↗.

Jesus restored Peter and gave him meaningful work to do. Peter’s failure became part of his story, but it did not become the end of his story.

When you fail:

  • Do not hide from the Creator.
  • Confess what happened.
  • Accept His forgiveness.
  • Learn what made you vulnerable.
  • Repair any harm you caused.
  • Make a practical plan for the next temptation.
  • Continue walking with Jesus.

Read 1 John 2:1 ↗ and Proverbs 24:16 ↗.

The enemy wants failure to become an excuse to quit. The Creator invites you to get up and continue.

What Does Obedience Have to Do With Change?

Jesus saves us by grace. Obedience does not purchase salvation.

Obedience shows that we trust Him.

Read John 14:15 ↗.

Love for Jesus creates a desire to follow His teachings. The Holy Spirit writes the Creator’s law upon the heart so that obedience becomes more than outward rule keeping.

Read Hebrews 8:10 ↗.

A changed heart begins to say:

“Creator, I trust that Your way leads to life. Teach me to walk in it.”

You may not understand every instruction immediately. Growth includes learning to trust the One who sees more than you can see.

Change Has a Purpose

The Creator is not changing you only for your own comfort.

Read Ephesians 2:10 ↗.

God created you for good works that He has prepared for your life.

Your healing can help you become a safe person for someone else.

Your freedom can bring hope to someone who feels trapped.

Your experience can help you recognize another person’s pain.

Your gifts can strengthen your family and community.

The Creator can redeem parts of your story that once seemed wasted.

Think About It

Write your answers in your own words.

  1. What label from your past has been difficult to release?
  2. What is the difference between outward behavior and a changed heart?
  3. What does it mean to be born again?
  4. Which fruit of the Spirit do you most want the Creator to grow in you?
  5. Is there a repeated thought that needs to be replaced with truth?
  6. What healthy family or cultural strength do you want to carry forward?
  7. Is there a harmful pattern you want to stop with your generation?
  8. What practical action could help you face your strongest temptation?
  9. Who is a safe person you could ask for support?

Try This During the Coming Week

Set aside ten quiet minutes each morning.

Begin with this prayer:

“Creator, give me a new heart today. Fill me with Your Spirit and help me choose Your way.”

Then read one passage:

  • Day 1: John 3:1–17 ↗
  • Day 2: Ezekiel 36:22–28 ↗
  • Day 3: John 15:1–11 ↗
  • Day 4: Romans 12:1–2 ↗
  • Day 5: Galatians 5:16–25 ↗
  • Day 6: Philippians 2:12–16 ↗
  • Day 7: John 21:15–19 ↗

After reading, write down:

  • What does the Creator want to change or grow in me?
  • What promise can I trust today?
  • What one choice will help me cooperate with Him?

Choose one small action and practice it each day. Lasting change often grows through small choices repeated with the Creator’s help.

A Prayer You Can Pray

Creator God, thank You that my past does not have to control my future. Give me the new heart You have promised. Fill me with Your Spirit and renew my mind through Your truth. Help me release harmful thoughts, habits, and patterns. Grow love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control within me. When I fall, help me return to You instead of hiding. Shape me into the person You created me to become, and use my life to bring healing and hope to others. Amen.

Remember This

Jesus offers more than forgiveness. He offers a new life.

The new birth is an inner change produced by the Holy Spirit.

Spiritual growth may begin quickly, but maturity develops over time.

You grow by staying connected to Jesus.

The Holy Spirit changes your desires and produces new fruit.

A new heart does not erase your Native identity.

Harmful patterns from the past do not have to control your future.

Temptation is not the same as sin.

Failure does not have to end your journey.

The Creator will continue His work as you trust and follow Him.
